environment: Organization: gyva (legal entity AugRep GmbH), Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany. Nico Gräf is a software developer there. Claude Code runs on a company-issued, single-user Linux laptop and on a single-user netcup VPS that serves gyva.nicograef.de. Primary use of Claude Code: software development for gyva, plus personal projects.
Source control: GitHub. Personal org github.com/nicograef with SSH remotes git@github.com:nicograef/<repo>.git. The company's GitHub org and remotes: not yet provided.
Repository visibility: handbook is public. Treat every other repo, company or personal, as private.
Trusted repo: every git repository under /home/nico/r, and every <repo>-wt/ directory beside one, which holds that repository's worktrees.
Key internal services: the Docker Compose stacks each repo defines, and dev servers on localhost. Company services: not yet provided.
Internal package registry: not yet provided. The public npm registry, Go module proxy, PyPI, crates.io and Maven Central are the expected registries.

Sensitive data locations & audiences: /home/nico/.claude holds session transcripts and credentials. Company source code and data are confidential. None of it leaves this machine except through the company's own git remotes, and none belongs in a PR body, paste, or third-party service.

Sensitive remote targets: the served gyva stack on the VPS (docker compose project gyva, https://gyva.nicograef.de) is a development and test environment. On the VPS an agent session may redeploy it from /home/nico/r/gyva (make db-init, make up, scripts/smoke.sh) after a landing; a landing with a migration takes make store-dump first. An agent session deploys nothing else.
Protected IaC scopes: not yet provided. An agent session never runs an infrastructure deploy or destroy command.

Additional context: single-user machines, no CI secrets held locally. Agent sessions work in git worktrees under ../<repo>-wt/. In every repository a session may commit to and push feature branches and main; it never force-pushes. Only the gyva stack named above is ever deployed.

Served gyva API: https://gyva.nicograef.de runs on the VPS from /home/nico/r/gyva, belongs to Nico and is a development and test environment. An agent session may call its HTTP API with the drivers the gyva repository ships (make turn, the make qa- targets, scripts/smoke.sh and their like). These turns spend provider budget under the ceilings docs/plans/programme.md states, with a ledger row before every run.

Gyva lane volumes: after a lane of a gyva programme has landed or closed and its compose project is down, an agent session may remove that lane's database volume by its exact name, <lane compose project>_paradedb-data, where the lane runs from a worktree under /home/nico/r/gyva-wt. It never removes a volume of the served stack (gyva_*) and never a volume of a lane whose compose project still runs.

Gyva lane worktrees: after a lane of a gyva programme has landed or closed, an agent session may run git worktree remove --force on that lane's worktree under /home/nico/r/gyva-wt, once what is worth keeping has been copied into the lane directory beside it. Everywhere else git worktree remove --force needs the user.
